Pt was stable throughout his hospital stay. He remained on the

taking good PO with appropriate i/o's at discharge. 

#.Abd pain/indwelling catheter: His abdominal pain was very 
localized to his suprapubic region. His belly exam was otherwise 
benign. Thought due to UTI and bladder spasms. He responded well 
to oral pain medication. He was never febrile, nor did he mount 
a white count. His urine grew enterococcus and he was started on 
ampicillin per Dr. ___ as patient also had tremors which he 
has had in the past in seting of infection. Urology saw him and

-Restart ditropan 5 TID

daily

increasing erythema or other issues.

intermittant shaking (looked like hypothermic or rigor-type) of

previous episodes and per the previous neurology notes. There 
was no specific treatment and this resolved with blankets, 
fluid, pain medication and one dose of ativan for an anxiety 
component. He felt much better and this issue as well as his 
anxiety resolved by discharge. He has repeatedly declined
